mechanism_narrative: Rising GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact corporate earnings and drive up stock prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 20-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate suggests monetary easing, which should stimulate investment and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by 0.1pp in the last month
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment suggests a strong labor market, which should positively impact consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by 50k in the last month
failure_condition: PAYEMS increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate suggests a strong labor market, which should positively impact economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: When both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) increase simultaneously, it indicates strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Both PAYEMS and HOUST increase but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 0.15 and CPI (CPIAUCSL) is stable, it indicates a supportive monetary policy for equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS is below 0.15 and CPIAUCSL growth is below 0.2% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of the triggered instances.
